paragraphs: Swamiji once travelled through the desert in western India, near the coast of the Indian Ocean. Day after day he walked on foot, and to his surprise he saw beautiful lakes every day, ringed with trees whose upside-down reflections trembled on the water. How lovely, he thought; and people call this a desert! For almost a month he journeyed on, enjoying these wonderful lakes and trees.

Then one day, very thirsty, he headed toward one of those clear lakes to drink. As he came closer, it simply disappeared. In a flash he understood: this was the mirage he had read about all his life. And he realised that every day of that month, he had been looking at mirages without knowing it.
The next morning he set out again. The lake was there as before, but now he knew it for what it was: a mirage, not water.

Swamiji said the universe is like this. We travel through the mirage of the world day after day and year after year, never suspecting it. Even after the illusion breaks, it returns, because the body is still under the power of past karma. People, animals, plants, our attachments and duties all come back to us, but they no longer hold the same power. With true knowledge, karma loses its grip and its poison. We now know the difference between what is real and what only looks real.
learn: Once you see through something, a toxic habit or a false promise, it may still show up in your life, but it cannot fool you the same way. Awareness does not make every problem vanish; it changes how much power it has over you.
